tags: Real photographs of the bottle and the notes
A tide chart for a day on skin
A bag that gives fill and arrival dates
features: The bottle and its price are on the first screen, so a visitor can buy without scrolling
A tide chart turns the notes into something you can feel through a screen: drag through eleven hours and each one rises as it leads
Three sizes and a bag that says when the bottle is filled and when it arrives, the two questions that stall a luxury order
A sample in every box and 30-day returns sit beside the button, right where the doubt is
name: Marée
short: Eleven hours on skin, drawn as five tides, from a one-scent house in Saint-Malo.
long: Marée sells one mineral extrait, so the page behaves like the sea it comes from. Drag through a day on skin and each note rises over its own photograph as it leads. Pick a size and the bag says when it is filled and when it arrives.
proves: A luxury brand can feel expensive and still get the bottle into the bag in two taps.
story: A one-scent fragrance house in Saint-Malo. Most perfume sites sell with gold and adjectives. This one sells with the sea: real photographs of every note, a tide chart for a day on skin, and a bag that answers when it ships.
